**Sikhae (Seafood Stew)** A classic Korean dish that's hearty, spicy, and perfect for cold days. Below you’ll find a basic recipe plus some optional tweaks so you can tailor it to your taste. --- ### Ingredients | Category | Item(s) | |-------------------|-----------------------------------------| | **Base & Broth** | • 1 L water or fish stock
• 2 tbsp Korean chili paste (**gochujang**)
• 1–2 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes (**gochuugaru**)
• 1 tsp soy sauce (optional)
• 1 tsp sesame oil | | **Protein** | • 200‑300 g mixed seafood (shrimp, squid, mussels, clams, octopus). Fresh is best; frozen works if thawed properly.
• Optional: sliced pork belly or thinly sliced beef for extra richness | | **Vegetables** | • ½ cup kimchi (cut into bite‑sized pieces)
• 1 small onion (thinly sliced)
• 1 carrot (julienned)
• 1 zucchini (half‑moon slices)
• 1/2 bell pepper (any color, julienned)
• 1 handful spinach or kale (roughly chopped)
• 1 scallion (white part only, cut diagonally) | | **Seasonings** | • 1 garlic clove (minced)
• 1 tsp ginger (grated)
• 1 tsp sugar (to balance acidity)
• Salt & black pepper to taste | | **Optional Extras** | • 1 egg (for poaching at the end)
• 1 tbsp fermented soybean paste (**doenjang**) for depth
• A splash of rice wine or mirin for sweetness | --- ### Equipment Needed * Large pot or Dutch oven * Cutting board + knife * Measuring spoons/spoons * Stirring spoon / ladle --- ### Step‑by‑Step Instructions #### 1️⃣ Prep Your Base 1. In the pot, bring the water/fish stock to a gentle boil. 2. Add the minced garlic, grated ginger, gochujang, gochuugaru, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar. Stir until everything dissolves evenly. 3. Let the broth simmer for ~5 minutes – this melds flavors before adding other ingredients. #### 2️⃣ Layer the Vegetables 1. Toss in the onions, carrots, zucchini, bell pepper, and kimchi first because they take longer to soften. 2. Cook for another 3–4 minutes until veggies start becoming tender but still hold shape. #### 3️⃣ Add Protein 1. If you're including meat (pork belly/beef), add it now—give it a minute to brown slightly. 2. Then drop in all the seafood. Seafood cooks fast, so keep an eye on them. 3. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Remember, the broth already has plenty of umami. #### 4️⃣ Finish With Greens Add the spinach/kale last, letting it wilt quickly (~30 seconds). It adds freshness and nutrients. #### 5️⃣ Poach Egg (Optional) If you love eggs in stews: 1. Crack one fresh egg directly into the bubbling liquid. 2. Cover the pot and let it steam for 2–3 minutes until whites set but yolk remains runny. #### 6️⃣ Final Touches Taste the soup. Adjust seasoning: more salt, a dash of vinegar, or a pinch of sugar depending on your palate. Give it a quick stir, then remove from heat. #### 7️⃣ Serve Hot! Transfer the sizzling stew into bowls. Garnish with a few scallions, maybe a drizzle of hot pepper oil, and serve immediately with steamed white rice or a side of pickled vegetables. --- ### Tips & Variations | Variation | How to Do It | |-----------|--------------| | **Spicier** | Increase gochugaru or add fresh sliced chilies while boiling. | | **Less Spicy** | Reduce gochujang/gochugaru amounts; use mild kimchi. | | **Meat‑Only Version** | Omit seafood entirely; replace with thick cuts of pork belly or beef brisket. | | **Vegan/Kosher** | Skip animal products; use tofu cubes instead of meat, and ensure all seasonings comply. | | **Broader Flavor Profile** | Add a tablespoon of doenjang during step 1 for deeper earthiness. | | **Quick Fix** | Use pre‑made seafood mix packs available in grocery stores; follow package directions for timing. | --- Enjoy crafting your own version of *sikhae*! Feel free to experiment with different combinations of seafood and veggies—you’ll discover new favorites along the way. Happy cooking!
